title: The Visitor's Eye Line
beat: PinPin admits that the quill's origin is a mystery, then asks how to learn its history.
camera: Move close to the visitor's position from the elder's side, 12 cm high, with the meadow behind.
staging: Reserve a low centre-right position for PinPin; the camera meets his eyes without making him stand upright.
alt: An intimate empty patch of the clearing with silver leaves, meadow light and a distant lake glimmer.

references.role: Location and framing reference; inspect before generation.

prompt: In this outward-looking clearing reference, move the camera forward about 60 cm toward the empty place where the visitor would be. Lower it to 12 cm above the ground and use a 65mm portrait field of view in a landscape frame. We look across a little patch of fine soil and fallen oak leaves toward the silver-green meadow; the plants beyond become softly detailed background, with only a tiny blue-green glimmer of lake far to the RIGHT. Keep a small section of the root at the extreme lower right as a continuity cue. The empty centre-right foreground is where a 25 cm hedgehog can rest with its face at lens height. Preserve the morning illumination from the left of this reversed view and gentle shadow detail. Landscape-only environment plate: plants, soil, stone and sky, with no animals, birds, insects or characters. Warm dimensional children's-book woodland, soft natural highlights and detailed green shadows. Single landscape 1536x1024, no text or panels.
review: The reverse portrait plate preserves the left fern, right root and distant lake, with a clear low patch for PinPin. No fauna visible. The field of view remains wider than a literal 65mm portrait; future character scale must be anchored to the leaves, not enlarged simply to fill the page. Background detail is gently softened rather than erased.
